values.goal: Understand the scene graph, model loading, and GPU resource lifetimes, and build a measurable 3D inspector.
values.capstone: A 3D inspector with model selection, camera fitting, animation, minimap, and error recovery, plus a resource and performance report

values.title: Scene Graphs and Cameras
values.prerequisites: You need to understand JavaScript ES modules, vector and matrix basics, and a first WebGL scene.
values.environment: The existing built-in example provides only a starting point. It does not implement all expanded requirements. Implement it yourself in an HTML and ES module project served by a separate local HTTP development server. Pin three and addons to the same installed version and record it.
values.concepts.0.title: Parent Transforms
values.concepts.0.explanation: A Group transform accumulates into its children’s world coordinates. A child position is relative to its parent, so it is not the same as a screen position.
values.concepts.1.title: View Direction and Position
values.concepts.1.explanation: The camera position and the point it looks at are different values. Changing FOV changes the projected size even when the position stays fixed.
values.outcomes.0: Print changes in local and world coordinates.
values.outcomes.1: Distinguish the effects of FOV from camera movement.
values.steps.0: Prepare day-01.js and index.html in the external exercise project. Add two Mesh objects to the Group in the existing threejs-01 and add an AxesHelper.
values.steps.1: Accept parent rotation and camera FOV as inputs, and display the getWorldPosition result in an HTML output.
values.steps.2: Save the output under the 0 input condition, then run again under the PI/2 condition. Expected: The child’s local coordinates stay the same, but its world coordinates rotate. Compare with the actual screen and logs, and record the actual result and reasons for any differences in day-01-notes.md.
values.variables.0.name: Parent rotation
values.variables.0.expected: The child’s local coordinates stay the same, but its world coordinates rotate.
values.criteria.0: Print changes in local and world coordinates.
values.criteria.1: Distinguish the effects of FOV from camera movement.
values.questions.0: Why does a child position stay unchanged when only its parent moves?
values.questions.1: How do lookAt and position differ?
